title: Refund endpoint lets any authenticated user refund another user's order (IDOR)

trace.description: id passed to findOrder() with no owner filter

evidence.description: Query is WHERE id = $1 with no user_id predicate

counterevidence: Checked requireAuth middleware (authenticates only) and the orders policy file; no ownership check on this route. Sibling GET /orders/:id does check ownership.

likelihood.reason: Any signed-up user can call it; order ids are sequential

impact.reason: Refunds another customer's payment; direct financial loss

conditions.description: Attacker needs any user account (open signup)

title: String-built SQL in product search

evidence.description: ORDER BY column interpolated into SQL

counterevidence: Column comes from a fixed enum map; user input never reaches the template literal.

ruled_out_by.control: SORT_COLUMNS allow-list lookup; unknown keys throw before the query is built

title: Link-preview fetcher may reach internal metadata endpoint (SSRF)
counterevidence: No allow-list in code. Egress may be filtered by the platform; not visible in the repo.
blockers: Whether the production egress proxy blocks 169.254.169.254 and RFC 1918 ranges
validation_plan: From a staging instance, request /preview?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ and confirm the response is blocked.
